subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw core own generic side-effect claim verification for Telegram/source-channel final text, or should core stay limited to delivery evidence and route generic claim verification to plugins or ClawHub?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans channel delivery, agent runtime state, and optional policy enforcement; source evidence shows partial core guardrails, while VISION.md and #68051 push broad claim verification toward plugins unless a missing core API is identified.

options.title: Keep Core Narrow
options.body: Core continues to enforce source-channel delivery invariants and exposes or documents the hooks needed for a claim-verification plugin.

options.title: Add Core Verification
options.body: Core implements a turn-level side-effect ledger and suppresses or flags success claims that are unsupported by tool evidence.

options.title: Force Tool-Only Telegram DMs
options.body: Telegram direct messages default to tool-only visible replies, reducing one false-success path but changing existing direct-chat behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep Core Narrow
recommendation.body: Core continues to enforce source-channel delivery invariants and exposes or documents the hooks needed for a claim-verification plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest policy trail from the closest merged guardrail and the related ClawHub scope decision.
